summary: CADCraft v0.10.0 (released 2026-10-19/21) is a pre-alpha, pure-Rust, MIT/Apache-2.0 2D CAD app targeting AutoCAD 2027 parity. Measured on 2026-10-21 from the clone at /home/user/cadcraft_1 without building: 193,684 lines of Rust in 618 files across 12 library crates + 3 apps + xtask; 413 registered engine command ids (240 with interactive prompt machines) plus 56 UI-only commands; 2,184 #[test] attributes; 16 interface languages. The repo's own weighted self-assessment: menu breadth 245/491 = 50% (ROADMAP, 2026-10-10; the regenerated checklist of 2026-10-16 says 283/491 = 58%), ready for real work ≈ 38%, mainstream 2D drafter ≈ 28%, essentials user ≈ 46%; DXF ≈ 50% read / 30% write, DWG ≈ 30% read / 15% write; 3D 2%; stability 35%. Strong: 2D draw/modify/dimension/layer/hatch/block basics, parametric constraints, DXF foreign-data round trip, vector PDF with real text and layers, cross-platform signed builds incl. Linux/FreeBSD/web, agent-first automation (MCP, JSON control channel, CLI), AutoLISP core, and a credible never-crash architecture (unsafe forbidden, panic lints, catch_unwind guards that restore the drawing, ~40 hostile-input tests, caps everywhere, autosave with recovery, AUDIT/RECOVER). Weak: 4 of 5 daily workflows fail its own alpha gate; DWG save is lossy via the acadrust bridge and never verified in AutoCAD with no real-file corpus; no 3D, no civil/land features whatsoever (zero hits for TIN/contour/alignment/COGO/GIS/geolocation/survey in the code); no PDF/raster underlays, SHX fonts, binary CTB/PC3, printers, sheet sets, eTransmit, fields, dynamic-block authoring, XCLIP, plug-in API; no CI test gate on PRs; absolute geometry tolerances and a 2D kernel untested at survey-scale coordinates; several parity docs contradict each other.

unique_strengths: Credible never-crash engineering: pure Rust with unsafe forbidden, panic-denying lints on 15 crate roots, 19 catch_unwind boundaries that restore the drawing, ~40 hostile-input tests plus a property-based numeric suite, caps on every input-sized structure, autosave with instance lock files, AUDIT/RECOVER that never guess content, crash-surviving rotated logs.

Agent-first automation no commercial CAD ships natively: MCP server (headless or bridged to the app), JSON control channel with UI introspection and screenshots, cadcraft-cli batch runs, and an 'everything is a command' registry whose JSON form never opens dialogs.
Broadest platform reach of the three apps compared: signed Windows x64/arm64/x86, notarized macOS universal, Linux (AppImage/Flatpak/deb/rpm, aarch64, riscv64), FreeBSD, and a browser build.

Free and open (MIT OR Apache-2.0), clean-room, no account; DXF foreign-data round trip (#528), vector PDF with real text/layers/hyperlinks, SVG import/export, own parametric solver with DOF reporting, 16 interface languages.
Swappable UI enforced by a layering gate; copy-on-write document with cheap undo; R-tree picking at 200k entities; extreme development velocity with honest, weighted self-assessment docs.
notable_weaknesses: Pre-alpha: 4 of 5 daily AutoCAD workflows fail the repo's own alpha gate; ready-for-real-work ≈ 38%, mainstream 2D drafter ≈ 28%.

DWG save is lossy through the third-party acadrust bridge, never verified in AutoCAD, no real-file corpus; a 10 MB DWG failed after ~2 minutes; DWG passes through an in-memory DXF (1.2 GB for an 83 MB file).
No 3D at all (2D Vec2 kernel, no UCS) and no civil/land-development capability of any kind (points/surfaces/contours/alignments/grading/parcels/GIS/geolocation/survey all absent).

No PDF/raster/DWF/DGN underlays or image display (ATTACH is a stub), no SHX fonts (text metrics differ), binary CTB/STB/PC3 unreadable, no physical printers, no sheet sets/eTransmit/fields/SPELL, no dynamic-block authoring or XCLIP, no plug-in API or CUI.
Stability self-rated 35% with no CI test gate on pull requests; ~400 open PRs and ~390 open issues on the upstream page (unverified); Windows/Linux lightly tested; web build lacks DWG and autosave.
Geometry on ellipses/splines is tessellated, tolerances are absolute, polyline offsets don't recompute bulges; untested at survey-scale coordinates.

Documentation drifts internally (lines of code 57k vs 194k; menu breadth 245 vs 283; UI/UX 43% vs 48%; languages table lists existing catalogs as 'none'; hardware doc says no 3D mouse while code exists).

genesis_relevant_findings.finding: Paths stored in a drawing (xrefs, data links) reach the file system only through one resolver: relative to the drawing's folder, refusing network hosts other than the drawing's own share, refusing relative paths when the drawing is unsaved; a refused path behaves like a missing file with the reason in the xref status. Keep and extend into a declared project container.

Resolution order (as given, then by file name beside the host), nested attach-only loading to depth 16, circular-reference guard, caps of 4M objects / 1,000 files / 512 MiB per file / 1 GiB total, symbols renamed xref|name, and the rule that an xref failure never stops the host from opening. Keep.
Unloaded state and per-xref layer overrides last only for the session; XCLIP doesn't exist; in-place xref edits aren't written back. Genesis must save xref state and clip boundaries in the document.

DATALINK reads CSV/TSV only (8 MiB cap), no Excel, no write-back, not on web; links, cell styles and breaks travel as app-private xdata and vanish through DWG; formulas aren't FIELDs so other tools see values. Genesis needs an open, bidirectional link model stored in a documented sidecar or native object, never private xdata.

Clipboard carries referenced layers, linetypes, styles and nested blocks; target keeps its own definition on a name clash, anonymous blocks are renamed, pasted objects get new handles; DXF text on the system clipboard enables cross-window paste; 50k-object cap. IMPORT merges a whole file's model space. Keep the explicit collision rule but surface it to the user.
Other programs' table-record and object handles are renumbered on CADCraft's first save; only entity handles survive. 'Better referencing' requires IDs that are never renumbered.

genesis_relevant_findings.topic: Lossless save as a day-one design
genesis_relevant_findings.finding: The top-ranked gap is 'saving DWG drops what we don't model'; DXF pass-through of unknown data was retrofitted (#528) but the DWG bridge still drops custom-class objects, xdata on tables/blocks, colour books and reactors, and output was never checked in AutoCAD. Genesis should treat unknown data as opaque pass-through from the first commit and run an external validator plus a real-file corpus in CI.
COMPARE matches by geometry/properties then handle, with a 200k-object cap, active layout only, no exportable report. Keep the matching idea; add per-layout, exportable diffs.

unsafe forbidden + panic lints; catch_unwind at command execute (restores drawing and selection), every interactive step (factory/begin/input/prompt/preview/drag), file open, the third-party DWG bridge, LISP and the render thread; copy-on-write undo makes restore trivial; hostile-input tests; input caps everywhere; autosave .sv$ with heartbeat lock files so only a crashed instance's files are offered; AUDIT/RECOVER that never guess.

No CI runs the tests on PRs (new nix.yml only evaluates the flake); stability self-rated 35%; web build has no autosave; autosave writes DXF not DWG; GPU-driver crashes are dodged by backend choice (DX12 only) rather than handled; DWG panics are caught but DWG data loss is not.

genesis_relevant_findings.topic: Tolerance model and 3D for land development
genesis_relevant_findings.finding: One absolute EPS = 1e-9, absolute tessellation steps (1e-3/1e-4 world units) and a 2D Vec2 kernel that discards Z; large UTM/state-plane coordinates are untested in commands. Genesis needs 3D points, a tolerance context relative to extents, and known-answer tests at 1e6–1e7 coordinates from the start.
genesis_relevant_findings.evidence: docs/geometry-parity.md Numbers and tolerances; docs/architecture.md Data model

genesis_relevant_findings.finding: Every user action is a CommandSpec with a JSON form that never opens dialogs; menus, toolbar, scripts, CLI, control channel and MCP hit the same registry; layering is enforced by cargo xtask layers so the UI is swappable. This gives automation, testability and agent control for free. Keep.

An 83 MB DWG with 888,483 orphaned DGN line-style components (a common site-plan artefact) only opens because such components are dropped before the DXF bridge; DWG passes through a 1.2 GB DXF in memory. Genesis needs a native, streaming DWG/DXF path rather than a text bridge.
